requirement: A living colony in the leaf litter. Follow the moving leaves.
fact: Leafcutters grow a fungus on harvested vegetation. The fungus is their food crop; a leaf is the beginning of a garden.
signal: Chemical trails connect the colony to its forage.
uncertainty: Colony behavior is sourced; colony size and trail geometry are stylized.

requirement: Support native stems to 60% and retain at least 50% canopy. Chemical vision leads to the hidden stem.
fact: Treehoppers communicate through plant-borne vibrations. A living stem carries a conversation that air alone cannot tell you.
signal: A repeating duet travels down the stem.
uncertainty: Communication is documented. Exact Monteverde occurrence, host identity, and elevation need field review. Numerical habitat rules are game abstractions.

requirement: In lower montane forest, restore flowering cover to 65%. Listen for activity among the stems.
fact: Bombus ephippiatus is a Central American bumblebee. The game's UV sense draws on bee vision; it is a translation for human eyes.
signal: Flowers become a landscape of contrasting guides.
uncertainty: Taxonomy is sourced. Species-specific UV patterns and local flower associations are not verified. The vibration discovery is a game convention.

requirement: Upper montane: retain 65% canopy and 60% flowering cover. Look beneath a leaf in UV vision; this resting adult opens the night layer.
fact: This tiger moth is known for ultrasonic clicks that interfere with bat sonar. Here, slowed synthetic pulses make that otherwise inaudible exchange perceptible.
signal: Clicks interrupt the sweeping bat pulse.
uncertainty: Sonar jamming is experimentally documented. Placement in this cloud-forest elevation is provisional, not a verified Monteverde occurrence.

requirement: At night in upper montane forest, maintain 65% moisture and 55% deadwood. Ultrasound makes the concealed movement legible.
fact: The golden appearance of this scarab comes from the organization of its cuticle. Its reflected light has unusual polarization properties.
signal: The shell resolves into bands of changing polarized light.
uncertainty: Optical structure is studied. Granting polarization vision does not establish that this species sees circular polarization. Its sound cue and habitat thresholds are fictionalized.

requirement: Restore flowering cover to 65% in premontane forest, then follow fragrance in chemical vision.
fact: Male orchid bees collect environmental fragrances. Their scent world reveals relationships that are easy to miss with sight alone.
signal: A fragrant plume curls from flower to bee.
uncertainty: Fragrance behavior is supported at the orchid-bee group level; the exact blend and local flower partners are not specified.

requirement: Restore native host stems to 65%, canopy to 55%, and moisture to 50%. Tend the resulting larva for eight game days, then document the adult.
fact: Morpho helenor larvae are recorded on several host plants in Costa Rica. The notebook adult is earned by keeping a developing larva safely sheltered.
signal: Blue flashes alternate with the resting outline of a leaf.
uncertainty: ACG documents this species and its life cycle. Eight-day development and generic host planting are compressed game rules, not rearing instructions.

requirement: At the elfin ridge, use polarization with canopy at 55% or more. This is a second behavioral plate of the golden scarab, not an additional species.
fact: A familiar animal becomes a new discovery in another sensory world. The ridge study records the shell's changing optical signature.
signal: Rotating bands reveal an animal against the open sky.
uncertainty: Ridge placement and the visualization are interpretive. A distinct color morph or separate species is not claimed.
